\section{Additional methods figures}
\label{app:methods-figures}

\subsection{Regressions}
\label{app:methods-figures-regressions}

% Checked 2026-10-26: the CH_4 regression shown is the one used for the published data
% (the slope implied by the published L data, -0.74943 yr / Mt CH_4, matches the re-derived regression exactly).
% It uses all historical years in which the first PC isn't constant (1750-2023),
% so it mixes the period where the historical first PC comes from the optimisation against ice cores (before 1948)
% with the period where it comes from the regression against emissions.
% Its slope is also around 5.6 times that of the historical dataset's regression against PRIMAP-hist (-0.135 yr / Mt CH_4).
% ZNTODO: wherever we refer to this regression (here and in Sect. \ref{sssec:methods-ch4-project-seasonality-lat-gradient}),
% refer to the discussion of inconsistencies between inputs (Sect. \ref{sec:discussion}).

We re-derive the regressions for CO_2, CH_4 and N_2O only.
For the other gases, we use the regressions from the historical dataset \citep{nicholls_historical-ghgs_2026} directly,
so they are not shown here.

\begin{figure}[hbt!]
\includegraphics[width=12cm]{@co2-regressions-figure@}
\caption{
    Regressions we re-derive for the CO_2 projections
    (Sect.~\ref{sssec:methods-co2-project-seasonality-lat-gradient}).
    a) Seasonality change PC from the historical dataset
    against MAGICC's median net primary productivity (NPP).
    b) Latitudinal gradient PC0 from the historical dataset
    against the historical fossil CO_2 emissions which underpin the scenarios.
}
\label{fig:methods-regressions-co2}
\end{figure}

\begin{figure}[tp]
\includegraphics[width=6cm]{@ch4-regressions-figure@}
\caption{
    Regression we re-derive for the CH_4 projections
    (Sect.~\ref{sssec:methods-ch4-project-seasonality-lat-gradient}):
    latitudinal gradient PC0 from the historical dataset
    against the historical fossil CH_4 emissions which underpin the scenarios.
}
\label{fig:methods-regressions-ch4}
\end{figure}

\begin{figure}[tp]
\includegraphics[width=6cm]{@n2o-regressions-figure@}
\caption{
    Regression we re-derive for the N_2O projections
    (Sect.~\ref{sssec:methods-n2o-like-project-seasonality-lat-gradient}):
    latitudinal gradient PC0 from the historical dataset
    against the historical total N_2O emissions which underpin the scenarios.
}
\label{fig:methods-regressions-n2o}
\end{figure}

\subsection{Extension of the Western et al. (2024) projections}
\label{app:methods-figures-western-et-al-2024}

\begin{figure}[hbt!]
\includegraphics[width=12cm]{@western-et-al-2024-extensions-figure@}
\caption{
    Extension of the \citet{western_hcfcs_2024} projections beyond 2100
    (Sect.~\ref{sssec:methods-cfc12-like-project-global-mean}).
    a, b) HCFC-22, c, d) HCFC-141b, e, f) HCFC-142b.
    a, c, e) Global-, annual-mean concentrations:
    the \citet{western_hcfcs_2024} projection (to 2100) and our extension of it (after 2100),
    alongside the historical dataset and the \citet{wmo_ozone-ch7_2022} projection, for reference.
    b, d, f) Emissions: the emissions implied by the \citet{western_hcfcs_2024} projection (to 2100)
    and the constant emissions which drive our extension (after 2100).
    The steps of the extension, numbered in a) and b), are the same for each gas:
    1) we invert the \citet{western_hcfcs_2024} projection with a one-box model (Eq.~(\ref{eq:one-box})),
    2) we hold the resulting emissions in 2100 constant
    and 3) we run the one-box model forward from 2100 with these constant emissions.
}
\label{fig:methods-western-et-al-2024}
\end{figure}

\section{MAGICC compared with our concentrations for the gases which use a single concentration projection}
\label{app:magicc-mismatch}

For the gases which use a single concentration projection,
MAGICC is run with the official emissions, including the official extensions beyond 2100,
which differ from the emissions implied by our concentrations after 2100
(Sect.~\ref{sssec:methods-cfc12-like-project-global-mean}).
The figures in this appendix show the size of this difference for each gas.

@magicc-mismatch-appendix-figures@
